steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Excuse me, Chief? Has my application been approved?
The boy in the chair asks as soon as the door of the interrogation room slides open.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm very sorry. Your application cannot be approved at this time.
You sit down and gaze at the mountain of folders on the table before you.
Many Sinners' files have tested your patience before, but this boy in front of you, Kawa-kawa, truly has too many violation records.
Yet each case seems so... Uncharacteristic for a Sinner.
You really want to ask the Public Security Bureau why so many minutiae count as "violations".

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I still have important work to do in WhiteSands. How about we give each other a break and stop wasting each other's time.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Alright, Chief?
The blue-haired boy probably thinks the thick stack of files on the table are his applications, so he's trying again.
Kawa-kawa guided the investigation team during the WhiteSands operation. He led the sand ship in the right direction and came to your rescue just in time before the ruins collapsed.
Yet now it seems there are some problems with this talented guide.
Moreover... He doesn't seem to know what's going on.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: First of all, are you aware of your current situation? As in, the reason why you're held here.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Of course I'm aware!
His face glows with confidence.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I recently used my power to make some more beacons. I could've hurt myself by using my power like that.
It seems that he has no idea that he'd be detained as a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Also, other people don't seem to like me very much...

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Not really... It's just that... I don't know how to describe it...

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I wanted to befriend them, but for some reason, no one really gets close with me...

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Some even came up to me and asked, "Are you actually a scapegoat for someone else?"

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: That's why I've been submitting so many applications. I really have a lot of mapping work to do.

options: This boy has no idea about the situation he's in.

choices.text: This boy has no idea about the situation he's in.

steps.content: It seems he won't be able to integrate with the other Sinners for a while.
The boy has no record of using his Sinner power to hurt others.
He doesn't belong here. He shouldn't even be in DisCity. He only belongs to the boundless WhiteSands.
We'll talk about all your cases later. It seems that I should first explain to you the purpose of this facility.
The MBCC's duty is to detain and manage Sinners. We have both the obligation and capacity to prevent the worst scenarios from unfolding.
Upon hearing this, the blue-haired boy frowns.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Chief, I really wish you used simpler words.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Tell it to me in a way that's easy to understand, like when I told you that people get eaten if they get too close to sandworms.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In DisCity, Sinners have to stay here for interrogation. because Sinners are dangerous.
For a moment, the boy seems to get it, but he is soon overcome with new confusion again.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: But... I've never done anything that can harm others. I just want to finish mapping WhiteSands and then mark the safe routes with beacons.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I'm trying to protect others, just like what we were doing in WhiteSands. Why do I need to be locked up?

options: You're doing it the wrong way.

choices.text: You're doing it the wrong way.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're doing things in a way that violates official regulations and creates chaos for other agencies.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The chaos you've created has done more harm than good. It takes a lot to clean up after you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Take a look at this.
test
test
test
test
test
test
The screen in the interrogation room begins to play a video.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You repeatedly entered the official base station in WhiteSands without permission and misappropriated supplies for personal use. By law, you're guilty of theft and trespassing.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Theft? Trespassing? I'm not sure I know what that means...
The boy's amber eyes show no sign of panic. It seems he has long taken these things for granted.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: If you're talking about the food and water at the base station, I did use some of it, but isn't that really normal?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: People living in WhiteSands always help each other out. I saw that no one has used those supplies for a long time. Some boxes are almost even buried.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: If someone is in urgent need of food, isn't it necessary to use the supplies?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Many people aren't familiar with the WhiteSands and they get lost, while I know where the base stations are and how to get to them safely. It's only natural for me to help them.
Kawa-kawa has mentioned "many people". And many in WhiteSands who need help don't live in shelters with stable shields.
Some are homeless refugees, but others are the desert bandits who you were so close to eradicating.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: According to our investigation, many of those you've helped are desert bandits. You've handed over valuable government resources to the desert bandits who sowed chaos in WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is also the most important reason for detaining you. Abetting desert bandits is a serious crime.

options: You helped those who shouldn't have been helped.

choices.text: You helped those who shouldn't have been helped.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu appears completely oblivious to your implied meaning, merely shaking her head slowly with a tinge of reproach and forgiveness in her eyes.
steps.content: But... They're not like those scary bandits... Chief, quit saying stuff that I don't understand!

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: All I know is that, if someone is dying of thirst in WhiteSands, I have to give them water to drink.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I know my way around WhiteSands, but others don't. If I didn't help them, they wouldn't have survived till sunset.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: The people who arrested me are just like you. All you talk about is the law.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: To make things worse, they knocked over my water flask! That whole big flask of water, all gone! Do you know how many people that amount of water could've saved?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I shouldn't have helped you back in WhiteSands!
The boy seems to be quite angry.
You take a deep breath, your mind whirring. It seems you've underestimated the boy's lack of common sense. You must tone down your expectations even more.

options: Can you tell me about those people?

choices.text: Can you tell me about those people?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Uh... why do you suddenly ask that?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So that I can brief our operatives. According to you, everyone in WhiteSands helps each other out, so maybe we won't have any conflict next time we run into those "friends" of yours.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: You promise? It'd be really nice if there are fewer conflicts. But everyone dresses pretty much the same in WhiteSands. There's just a few types of desert uniforms.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did their clothes have any insignia? Or were they carrying... certain weapons?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Ah! Now that you mention it, I remember I did meet a group of travelers whose cloaks were buttoned with dagger-shaped pins.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are these the guys?

You press the remote control. The screen is still showing surveillance footage, but the scene has changed to a sand cruiser anchored in WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Take a close look. Are the people on the left side of the screen the travelers you helped?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I think... It might be them. But I can't see their faces clearly, so I'm not sure.
You remain silent, waiting for the images to change.
The video begins to play. Several cloaked figures with long knives and submachine guns climb onto the main deck of the cruiser with hook locks.

steps.speaker: Crew Member
steps.content: Wh-who are you?
A crewman steps out of the bridge to see what's going on, but he is greeted by a hail of bullets.
Kawa-kawa's stomach twitches when he sees the crewman's body slump over by the bloodstained porthole.
But the boy holds back from vomiting on the spot. The footage dissolves into static as the bullets pulverize the surveillance cameras.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This video is from a month and a half ago. Desert bandits attacked a sand cruiser in WhiteSands. By the time the patrol team received the distress signal and rushed to the scene, no survivors were found.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There were twenty-three crew members in total. The desert bandits snatched away everything they could take, sparing not even the crew's personal belongings.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The cruel environment of WhiteSands may unite those living there, but it can also make them cruel.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: No... no! How can this be?
What he believed to be good deeds have reaped horrific results. The boy is deeply confounded.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm just stating a fact. Not everyone in WhiteSands is as kind or eager to help others as you are.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: People who slaughter innocents without batting an eye like these desert bandits make strict laws necessary.

options: Some people don't deserve your kindness.

choices.text: Some people don't deserve your kindness.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Then what... what should I do?
The rehabilitation is beginning to pay off. However, the boy won't be able to accept everything all at once. You can see the denial, confusion, and a hint of unease in his eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Next time someone asks you for help, at least ask them a few questions about their background.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you encounter any suspicious individuals who might be desert bandits, alert us right away. The patrol team in WhiteSands will go and catch them.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Alright, I'll listen to you. Then what if I...

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Wait a sec.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: What did you just say? Next time?
The boy's crestfallen eyes suddenly flash with exuberance.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: So you've agreed to let me out?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: However, the MBCC will soon organize another cleansing operation against the desert bandits. I will put you on the task force.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If things go well, I'll arrange for you to continue data collection along the way. You'll also be able to place your beacons.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Awesome!

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: There's an area of WhiteSands that I'm almost finished mapping! I just need one more round of data collection to complete it!
As the boy cheers, the brief interrogation comes to an end.
The boy is soon taken out of the interrogation room, while you return to your office. At least on the surface, everyone is happy with the outcome.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief... should we believe him so easily?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The cleansing operation has entered the final stage of planning. Isn't it too risky to include such an unpredictable element?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Relevant agencies are already working overtime to analyze the weather data of WhiteSands for this operation.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: With experience from the last operation, we do not necessarily need a navigator.
You understand what Nightingale is getting at. There had been too many blunders in the previous WhiteSands operation.
With regards to the upcoming WhiteSands operation, it is only natural to try and minimize unpredictable elements as much as possible.

options: He is first and foremost a geologist.

choices.text: He is first and foremost a geologist.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: He is a navigator second, and a Sinner last.

The data from the beacons, combined with the strange forecasting model, are indeed more accurate than the research institutes' forecasts, no? He claims to be a geologist, and so far, there's no evidence to disprove that.

It's just like what the boy has always insisted. A search of his carry-on luggage has revealed many research materials on the geology and climate of WhiteSands, as well as hundreds of WhiteSands maps with surveying data.
To most people, those maps all look exactly the same.
Among the materials, there is a thick notebook documenting a very complex dynamic theoretical model.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After reviewing the theoretical model, the only conclusion the research institutions can draw is that it's a model that tries to predict the weather changes in WhiteSands. However, without enough real-time data to back it up, it remains of dubious value.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: That theoretical model does hold some value, but we can't rule out the possibility that Kawa-kawa is an accomplice of the desert bandits. Like you said, he claims to be a geologist.
Nightingale emphasizes the words "claims to be" extra hard.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But is there any other, better way? If the forecasting system used by the fleet can avoid sandstorms, we naturally wouldn't need a navigator.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for socializing him with reality, he has to personally experience things to truly understand the ways of the world, no?
